WITH ls AS (
 SELECT DISTINCT gm.GAME_ID FROM CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.GAME_MODES gm
 JOIN CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.GAME_MONETIZATION gmo ON gmo.GAME_ID=gm.GAME_ID
 JOIN CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.MONETIZATION_TYPES mt ON mt.MONETIZATION_ID=gmo.MONETIZATION_ID
 WHERE gm.ONLINE_REQUIRED=TRUE AND mt.MONETIZATION_NAME IN ('battle_pass','microtransactions','subscription','loot_boxes')),
mon AS (SELECT gmo.GAME_ID, LISTAGG(DISTINCT mt.MONETIZATION_NAME, ', ') WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY mt.MONETIZATION_NAME) models,
 MAX(IFF(mt.MONETIZATION_NAME='loot_boxes',1,0)) lb FROM CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.GAME_MONETIZATION gmo JOIN CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.MONETIZATION_TYPES mt ON mt.MONETIZATION_ID=gmo.MONETIZATION_ID GROUP BY 1),
pegi AS (SELECT gr.GAME_ID, MAX(ar.MIN_AGE) pegi_age FROM CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.GAME_RATINGS gr JOIN CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.AGE_RATINGS ar ON ar.RATING_ID=gr.RATING_ID WHERE ar.RATING_SYSTEM='PEGI' GROUP BY 1),
mob AS (SELECT gp.GAME_ID, 1 mobile FROM CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.GAME_PLATFORMS gp JOIN CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.PLATFORMS p ON p.PLATFORM_ID=gp.PLATFORM_ID WHERE p.PLATFORM_NAME IN ('Android','Apple') GROUP BY 1)
SELECT g.*, m.models, p.pegi_age, COALESCE(mb.mobile,0) mobile, m.lb,
 CASE WHEN p.pegi_age>=18 OR (m.lb=1 AND mb.mobile=1) THEN 'HIGH' ELSE 'ELEVATED' END tier
FROM ls JOIN CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.GAMES g ON g.GAME_ID=ls.GAME_ID
LEFT JOIN mon m ON m.GAME_ID=ls.GAME_ID LEFT JOIN pegi p ON p.GAME_ID=ls.GAME_ID LEFT JOIN mob mb ON mb.GAME_ID=ls.GAME_ID

rules.label: Fiscal Year
rules.rule: Fiscal year equals calendar year (January 1 through December 31). This fiscal year = YEAR(CURRENT_DATE()). Next fiscal year = YEAR(CURRENT_DATE()) + 1. Last fiscal year = YEAR(CURRENT_DATE()) - 1.

rules.label: Release Date
rules.rule: CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.GAMES.RELEASE_DATE is a DATE column. Use it directly in date functions like YEAR(), QUARTER(), DATEDIFF() without TRY_TO_DATE(). Use RELEASE_DATE for all time-based filtering of games.

rules.label: Publisher And Studio Names
rules.rule: Publisher and studio names differ between schemas. CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_SALES.TITLES.PUBLISHER_LABEL = 'SIE' and CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.GAMES.PUBLISHER_NAME = 'Sony Interactive Entertainment' are the same publisher. TITLES.STUDIO uses spaces ('Naughty Dog') and GAMES.DEVELOPER_NAME uses underscores ('Naughty_Dog') for the same studio. To combine sales and catalog data, join by ID through SELECT DISTINCT TITLE_ID, CATALOG_GAME_ID FROM CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_SALES.TITLE_CODE_XREF, then CATALOG_GAME_ID = GAMES.GAME_ID; never join PUBLISHER_LABEL to PUBLISHER_NAME or STUDIO to DEVELOPER_NAME. When a user names a publisher or studio, filter each schema using its own form: 'Sony', 'SIE' or 'Sony Interactive Entertainment' means PUBLISHER_LABEL = 'SIE' in GAME_SALES and PUBLISHER_NAME = 'Sony Interactive Entertainment' in GAME_CATALOG; a studio name is used as typed for TITLES.STUDIO and with spaces replaced by underscores for GAMES.DEVELOPER_NAME. Display developer names with REPLACE(DEVELOPER_NAME, '_', ' '). All titles in this data belong to Sony Interactive Entertainment, so there are no competitor publishers to compare against; say so if asked.

rules.label: Revenue Analysis
rules.rule: Revenue by title, gross vs net, and total company revenue are modeled in CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_SALES.SV_GAME_SALES; follow it. Lifetime game revenue is CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_SALES.GAME_REVENUE.INCOME (digital gross revenue, one row per TITLE_ID); it excludes hardware and subscriptions. For revenue by franchise, publisher, developer or indie vs studio, map titles with SELECT DISTINCT TITLE_ID, CATALOG_GAME_ID FROM CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_SALES.TITLE_CODE_XREF, join CATALOG_GAME_ID = CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.GAMES.GAME_ID, and group by GAMES.FRANCHISE_NAME, PUBLISHER_NAME, DEVELOPER_NAME or DEVELOPER_IS_INDIE. Never use TITLES.CATALOG_GAME_ID, and never join revenue to the xref without DISTINCT. Two titles have no catalog mapping; report them as 'Unmapped' so totals still match GAME_REVENUE. 'Top revenue earners' means ORDER BY INCOME DESC LIMIT 5 at title level; never apply a top-quartile or percentile cutoff unless the user asks.

rules.label: Genre Revenue
rules.rule: For revenue by genre, map revenue titles to catalog games with SELECT DISTINCT TITLE_ID, CATALOG_GAME_ID FROM CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_SALES.TITLE_CODE_XREF, then join CATALOG_GAME_ID to CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.GAME_GENRE_CLASSIFICATION.GAME_ID with MATCH_STATUS = 'FULL' (PARTIAL and NONE rows are not genre membership). Sum INCOME from CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_SALES.GAME_REVENUE and also report COUNT(DISTINCT GAME_ID) per genre. For broad or top-level genres (Action, Adventure, RPG, Horror, ...), use CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.VW_GAME_GENRE_ROLLUP (one row per GAME_ID and ROLLUP_GENRE, including parent genres; ROLLUP_DEPTH = 1 is top level) instead of GAME_GENRE_CLASSIFICATION. A game belongs to several genres (about 3 fully matched on average), so its full revenue counts in every genre it belongs to: genre totals add up to roughly 3 times total revenue and must never be presented as shares of total revenue or summed into a total. State this whenever genre revenue is shown. Ten mapped titles (about $2.8M) have no fully matched genre and two titles (about $230K) have no catalog mapping; report them as 'No full genre match' and 'Unmapped' rather than dropping them silently. For a single game's genre, use its fully matched genres only.

rules.label: Monthly Revenue Analysis
rules.rule: For monthly game revenue and lifecycle phases, use CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_SALES.MONTHLY_REVENUE as modeled in CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_SALES.SV_GAME_SALES. REVENUE_SOURCE is the monetization type, not a lifecycle phase; derive launch, early-life and tail phases from months since TITLES.RELEASE_DATE (a YYYYMMDD string). Sum MONTHLY_INCOME, never CUMULATIVE_INCOME. It is the same revenue as digital transactions; never add the two.

rules.label: Quarterly Revenue
rules.rule: For quarterly revenue, use CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_SALES.QUARTERLY_REVENUE which is a rollup of monthly data by REVENUE_YEAR and REVENUE_QUARTER (1-4). Use for YoY comparisons, trend analysis, and quarterly reporting.

rules.label: Time Series Best Practices
rules.rule: For monthly trends, SUM(MONTHLY_INCOME) GROUP BY REVENUE_MONTH from CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_SALES.MONTHLY_REVENUE. For quarterly trends, use CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_SALES.QUARTERLY_REVENUE and GROUP BY REVENUE_YEAR, REVENUE_QUARTER. For YoY comparison, compare same REVENUE_QUARTER across different REVENUE_YEARs. Derive launch windows from months since release as in CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_SALES.SV_GAME_SALES; never filter REVENUE_SOURCE for lifecycle phases.

rules.label: Exclusivity Revenue
rules.rule: To calculate revenue from exclusive titles, use CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_SALES.VW_PLATFORM_EXCLUSIVITY filtered to IS_CURRENTLY_EXCLUSIVE = TRUE; it already carries lifetime INCOME per TITLE_ID, so no join to GAME_REVENUE is needed. A title can have more than one exclusivity row, so count each TITLE_ID's INCOME once.

rules.label: Monetization Risk
rules.rule: To assess monetization risk, join CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_SALES.MONETIZATION_TYPES through CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_SALES.GAME_MONETIZATION to CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_SALES.VW_PLATFORM_EXCLUSIVITY on TITLE_ID to identify revenue concentration risks.

rules.label: Revenue By Monetization Model
rules.rule: Revenue by monetization model means the models tagged on each title, not transaction or product types. Join CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_SALES.GAME_MONETIZATION to CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_SALES.MONETIZATION_TYPES on MONETIZATION_ID, then to CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_SALES.GAME_REVENUE on TITLE_ID, and report SUM(INCOME) and COUNT(DISTINCT TITLE_ID) per MONETIZATION_NAME. Do not use DIGITAL_PRODUCT_TRANSACTIONS, DIGITAL_PRODUCTS or REVENUE_TYPES.MONETIZATION_TYPE for this. A title can use several models, so its full lifetime income counts under each one: totals overlap, must not be summed or shown as shares of total revenue, and the answer must say so.

rules.label: Content Rating Risk
rules.rule: A game poses a content rating risk when ANY of these apply: (1) MATURE RATING: MIN_AGE >= 16 in CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.AGE_RATINGS via CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.GAME_RATINGS (ESRB M/AO, PEGI 16/18, CERO D/Z); (2) VIOLENCE: a FULL match (MATCH_STATUS = 'FULL') for GENRE in ('Gore', 'Shooter', 'FPS', 'TPS', 'Fighting', 'Horror', 'SurvivalHorror') in CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.GAME_GENRE_CLASSIFICATION, or a 'Grotesque' theme (CONTEXT_NAME in ('monster_invasion', 'zombies_invasion') in CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.CONTEXTS via CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.GAME_CONTEXTS) combined with 'Combat' gameplay (GAMEPLAY_TYPE_NAME in ('agonistic', 'corpo_a_corpo', 'free_shooting') in CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.GAMEPLAY_TYPES via CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.GAME_GAMEPLAY); (3) ROMANTIC OR SEXUAL CONTENT: CONTEXT_NAME = 'romance' via GAME_CONTEXTS, GAMEPLAY_TYPE_NAME = 'romance_based' via GAME_GAMEPLAY, or a FULL match for GENRE = 'DatingSim'. Report which of the three criteria each game meets. There is no content-descriptor data, so violence and romance are inferred from genre, theme and gameplay, not stated; PEGI 16/18 descriptions mix violence and sexual content and cannot separate them. If no games meet the romance criterion, say so rather than inferring sexual content from the rating alone.

rules.label: EU Regulatory Risk
rules.rule: To assess EU regulatory risk, retrieve eu_regulatory_brief_loot_boxes.md and use it as the only source for the risk tiers, the conditions for each tier, the regulations and the required mitigations; do not answer from memory. Steps: (1) Identify live-service games first: ONLINE_REQUIRED = TRUE in CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.GAME_MODES AND recurring monetization (MONETIZATION_NAME in ('battle_pass', 'microtransactions', 'subscription', 'loot_boxes') in CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.MONETIZATION_TYPES via CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.GAME_MONETIZATION). (2) Apply the brief's tiers in order (HIGH, then ELEVATED, then WATCH) and give each game the first tier it meets. (3) Name the condition that triggered each tier and the regulation from the brief it relates to. (4) If no live-service game meets HIGH, say so plainly before reporting lower tiers. (5) Report the brief's required mitigations for each tier. (6) State that the brief is a simplified internal summary, not legal advice. To evaluate the brief's terms in the data: 'PEGI 18' = RATING_SYSTEM = 'PEGI' AND MIN_AGE >= 18 in CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.AGE_RATINGS via CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.GAME_RATINGS; 'paid loot boxes' = MONETIZATION_NAME = 'loot_boxes'; 'paid DLC' = MONETIZATION_NAME = 'dlc'; 'available on mobile' = PLATFORM_NAME in ('Android', 'Apple') in CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.PLATFORMS via CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.GAME_PLATFORMS. rules.label: Awards
rules.rule: For award analysis, use CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.GAME_AWARDS joined to CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.AWARDS. Filter WON_OR_NOMINATED = 'won' for wins only. Group by AWARDING_BODY for cross-award-show analysis.

Revenue tables in CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_SALES are keyed by TITLE_ID; map them to catalog games with SELECT DISTINCT TITLE_ID, CATALOG_GAME_ID FROM CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_SALES.TITLE_CODE_XREF, then CATALOG_GAME_ID = GAME_ID. Never present the proxy as an established fact.

rules.label: Emerging Genre
rules.rule: The data has no genre market-growth or demand data. When asked about emerging genres, state this first, then use a clearly labelled proxy: MARKET_STATUS = 'UNDERSERVED' or 'WHITESPACE' in CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.GENRE_WHITESPACE_ANALYSIS. Explain that this measures low game supply, not proven demand.

rules.label: Breakout Hit Prediction
rules.rule: A breakout hit achieves top-quartile INCOME in CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_SALES.GAME_REVENUE or wins Game_of_the_Year from any AWARDING_BODY in CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.GAME_AWARDS. This top-quartile threshold applies only to breakout hits; do not use it for 'top revenue earners'. The award-winning formula is computed by joining GAME_AWARDS (WON_OR_NOMINATED = 'won') through CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.GAMES to CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.GAME_GENRE_CLASSIFICATION, CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.GAME_MECHANICS, and CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.NARRATIVE_STRUCTURES. Compare indie studio trajectories (GAMES.DEVELOPER_IS_INDIE) against this formula. Revenue tables in CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_SALES are keyed by TITLE_ID; map them to catalog games with SELECT DISTINCT TITLE_ID, CATALOG_GAME_ID FROM CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_SALES.TITLE_CODE_XREF, then CATALOG_GAME_ID = GAME_ID.

rules.label: Release Calendar Optimization
rules.rule: For release calendar conflicts, analyze CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.GAMES.RELEASE_DATE grouped by YEAR and QUARTER. Two releases conflict when in same quarter AND WEIGHTED_OVERLAP >= 0.3 in CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.GAME_SIMILARITY_SCORES (check both GAME_A and GAME_B directions). Major release means top-quartile INCOME or franchise with 3+ titles; this threshold applies only to release planning, not to 'top revenue earners'. Join through CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.GAME_FRANCHISES to identify involved franchises. INCOME comes from CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_SALES.GAME_REVENUE. Revenue tables in CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_SALES are keyed by TITLE_ID; map them to catalog games with SELECT DISTINCT TITLE_ID, CATALOG_GAME_ID FROM CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_SALES.TITLE_CODE_XREF, then CATALOG_GAME_ID = GAME_ID.

rules.label: Accessibility Investment Priority
rules.rule: Rank accessibility features by a relative priority score: (count of games missing the feature from CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.VW_ACCESSIBILITY_GAPS) * (average INCOME of those games from CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_SALES.GAME_REVENUE). Present it as a ranking only; state that the data has no market-size or implementation-cost data and never report the score as dollar market or revenue impact. Group by FEATURE_CATEGORY. Prioritize gaps in Family/All-ages games (MIN_AGE <= 10 in CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.AGE_RATINGS via CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.GAME_RATINGS). Revenue tables in CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_SALES are keyed by TITLE_ID; map them to catalog games with SELECT DISTINCT TITLE_ID, CATALOG_GAME_ID FROM CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_SALES.TITLE_CODE_XREF, then CATALOG_GAME_ID = GAME_ID.

rules.label: Audience Comparison
rules.rule: When comparing whether two games target the same audience, ALWAYS check CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.GAME_SIMILARITY_SCORES for their WEIGHTED_OVERLAP score first. Each pair is stored in one direction only, so match GAME_A/GAME_B both ways. Cite the score and the OVERLAP_TIER column value (HIGH >= 0.6, MEDIUM 0.3 to under 0.6, LOW < 0.3); never re-derive the tier from thresholds. 'Highly cannibalized' means OVERLAP_TIER = 'HIGH'. Then supplement with audience dimension analysis from CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.GAME_GENRE_CLASSIFICATION (genre clusters), CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.GAME_PLATFORMS (platform reach), and CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.NARRATIVE_STRUCTURES (narrative style) to explain WHY they overlap or differ.

rules.label: Engine Revenue
rules.rule: Game engine data exists: CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.GAME_ENGINES maps each game to its engine (GAME_ID, ENGINE_ID, ENGINE_VERSION, CUSTOM_FORK), and CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.ENGINES holds ENGINE_NAME. For game counts by engine, join CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.GAME_ENGINES to CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_CATALOG.ENGINES on ENGINE_ID and COUNT(DISTINCT GAME_ID) by ENGINE_NAME. For revenue by engine, revenue tables in CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_SALES are keyed by TITLE_ID; map them to catalog games with SELECT DISTINCT TITLE_ID, CATALOG_GAME_ID FROM CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_SALES.TITLE_CODE_XREF, then CATALOG_GAME_ID = GAME_ID. Join that to GAME_ENGINES and ENGINES, then SUM(CORTEX_SENSE_DEMO.GAME_SALES.GAME_REVENUE.INCOME) grouped by ENGINE_NAME. Never say engine data is unavailable.
